sources.title: Before news broke of his affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Nvidia’s Huang told Fortune his company “could be of great service” to China
sources.text: Jensen Huang’s dealings with China and views on U.S. export controls on advanced AI chips are under fresh scrutiny after the Nvidia CEO confessed to an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies reportedly believe to be working as a spy for China. The U.S. has spent years restricting the sale of advanced Nvidia chips to China on national security grounds. In an interview Fortune conducted before the allegations surfaced, Huang said that he thought the chipmaker “could be of great service” to China. He also said that Nvidia had a “large and growing” opportunity in China. Huang spoke to Fortune in mid-October, before The New York Times first reported later that month that U.S. officials had concluded the woman, Alice Huang —who has no relation to the Nvidia CEO—was a Chinese intelligence asset. It isn’t clear how long the relationship lasted, but photos shared online show the two together in Taipei as early as June 2024. Asked in October whether he expected sales in China to pick up, Huang said there would be a “natural tension” between Washington and Beijing that “lasts a long time,” adding that Nvidia would continue to give shareholders no guidance on its China sales. The company has left China out of its revenue forecasts since August 2025, citing regulatory uncertainty in both countries. The U.S. has not allowed Nvidia to sell its most advanced AI chips to China, but has granted the company export licenses for older models of its graphics processing units (GPUs), the specialized chips that run AI and computer graphics applications. It has allowed Nvidia to market specialized versions of its GPUs in China that have been designed specifically for that market and which are engineered to be less capable at training frontier AI models. Beijing, for its part, has officially tried to bar the country’s major tech companies from buying Nvidia’s chips as part of an effort to spur demand for domestic alternatives. Nonetheless, Huang told Fortune he saw promise in the Chinese market. “I think the opportunity in China is large and growing, just like the AI market across the world is large and growing,” Huang said. “We could be of great service to the local market. We can compete and win as much of the AI market as possible for the United States, while also providing compute resources, which is really important to their economy.” China has been a long-running headache for Nvidia. Back in 2022, the Biden administration imposed export controls that barred Nvidia from selling its most advanced AI chips to China, aiming to slow Beijing’s progress in AI and its potential military applications. Nvidia designed scaled-down chips for the Chinese market, but successive rule changes cut many of those off too. Since then, Huang has continually pushed for more access to the Chinese market. In October 2025, after export controls and Beijing’s pushback had shut Nvidia out of the market, he complained that the company had gone from 95% market share in China to 0%. In December 2025, President Trump reversed course on some of the Biden-era restrictions, allowing Nvidia to ship its H200 chips—which are designed to comply with U.S. export controls—to approved Chinese customers, with the U.S. government taking a 25% cut. The decision came after months of lobbying by Huang, who met with Trump to discuss export controls days before the announcement. Nvidia’s complicated history with China has been dragged back into the spotlight by Huang’s confession to the extra-marital affair. In Sunday’s memo to staff reviewed by Fortune , he admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife, after the Financial Times reported on a U.S. government memo describing a romantic relationship between him and Alice Huang. “There is no excuse for what I did,” he wrote in the memo. “I am deeply sorry.” The same day, Nvidia’s board announced that a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, would examine whether company secrets or national security had been compromised. The board said it so far had “no reason to believe” either had been. For now, Huang remains CEO and said he would cooperate fully with the review. U.S. officials reportedly believe Alice Huang was working for China’s Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center operator where she was an executive, has become one of Nvidia’s largest customers over the past two years. Its Malaysian affiliate bought at least $4.8 billion in equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, according to the Times . U.S. officials have scrutinized the company since 2024 over suspicions it helped Chinese firms evade export controls. It is suspected that, despite U.S. export controls, the leading Chinese AI companies have access to large computing clusters of Nvidia’s advanced GPUs, obtained either through large-scale smuggling operations, or through data centers in other Asian nations that they have accessed using front companies. Nvidia has previously told news outlets that Huang’s dealings with Alice Huang were routine, and a company spokesperson told Fortune : “Today’s news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.” Megaspeed also did not respond to Fortune’s request for comment, and Alice Huang could not be reached. China’s foreign ministry called the allegations “pure groundless speculation and slander.” The Republican chairs of three House committees have asked Huang to attend a private briefing the day after Nvidia reports quarterly earnings next week. Lawmakers are likely to press Huang on whether his push into China has put U.S. interests at risk. In October, he told Fortune that Nvidia could put American customers first and still compete abroad. “The United States recognizes that because the technology is invented in the United States, and we’re an American company, we should provide, and we do provide, the best, the soonest and the most to American companies. sources.text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing an internal investigation after admitting to an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence agencies believe is a Chinese spy. While the company has not yet named specific investigators, that probe is being helmed by the board with help from outside counsel, according to Nvidia. Lawyer Stephen Neal is the board's lead independent director and head of corporate governance, likely making him a key figure in the investigation. In a statement , Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised," though it will examine all evidence. China has dismissed the espionage claims. Huang, one of the most powerful businessmen in the artificial intelligence boom, said he would "cooperate fully" with the process. Yet the probe has sparked uncertainty around Huang's future at the chipmaker and raised concerns of broader ripple effects to companies in the tech sector that are exposed to the AI build-out. In a Monday note, Citi analysts wrote that one of the key issues for investors moving forward will be "potential governance implications" and "increased regulatory scrutiny" as the company navigates the investigation. Nvidia's board has 10 independent members, including a former president of Taco Bell , a former Eli Lilly executive and a former vice chairman from Goldman Sachs . Neal, who joined Nvidia's board of directors in 2019, is a chairman emeritus and senior counsel of the law firm Cooley LLP, where he also served as CEO from 2001 to 2008. Neal did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It won't be his first corporate governance probe. According to Cooley , Neal has litigated cases across securities, bankruptcies, antitrust, takeovers and more. And he's conducted several investigations for multiple boards of directors, including at General Motors , where he advised the company in disputes with Ross Perot. He also guided Walter Hewlett and the Hewlett Trust to stop a merger between Hewlett-Packard Co. and Compaq Computer Corp. and helped PacifiCare Health Systems with transactional matters. According to the firm, Neal has conducted several investigations for committees of directors and independent directors, though most of those client names are confidential. He's also handled investigations with the Securities and Exchange Commission for both corporations and individuals. When he joined Nvidia, Neal was also the chairman of the board of directors at Levi Strauss & Co . He stepped down in 2021 after reaching the mandatory board retirement age of 72, the company said at the time. The retailer did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC on Monday. Cooley has a long history with Nvidia, too. The law firm said it incorporated the company in 1993 and has served as its principal outside corporate and litigation counsel for roughly three decades. Cooley handled Nvidia's initial public offering in 1999. Investors will be closely watching the investigation, and its emphasis on independence, as the process unfolds, according to Brayden King, a professor of management and organizations at Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management. "You definitely want somebody leading it who people can look at and say, 'OK, we believe this is a report that we can fully believe and trust that the outcome is the right outcome,'" King told CNBC. "That's what investors are looking for. They just don't like the instability that comes with all of this." King said the Nvidia investigation lies at a unique intersection of Wall Street and Washington, D.C., where the company is likely navigating its next steps to try to appease both groups. Because Nvidia's reputation is highly correlated with Huang's reputation, King said, conducting a transparent investigation will be key to regaining and retaining shareholders' trust. Not having an immediate CEO succession plan in place is only impeding that confidence, he added. "I think the board realizes that they're doing an independent investigation in part because they really need to understand to what extent there are real problems here, and they also know that if they don't do an independent investigation, then there will be lingering concerns about whether their key stakeholders can trust the company," King said. If the investigation shows that national security was indeed put at risk, King said, the company will need to take "very strong measures" to restore its reputation. "That will basically come down to having to put structures in place in corporate governance to assure that this can't happen again," King said. "The independent review is going to have to be truly independent, and it's going to have to be candid enough that people believe that we can restore some normalcy around how the company operates." It's also likely influencing how other tech companies, particularly those in the AI space, are thinking about their own corporate governance structures and how they might navigate increased scrutiny on their leaders, he added. Marcel Kahan, a professor of law at New York University, said he's not surprised that Nvidia has been potentially exposed to industrial espionage. Because the company operates in such a high-visibility and crucial sector, Kahan said companies like Nvidia have to be careful in their operations and whom they trust with their information. sources.title: Jensen Huang affair puts Nvidia's future at risk, with no clear successor to the renowned CEO
sources.text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's admission of an affair with a purported Chinese spy has raised questions about his future at the company, and what happens if the 63-year-old co-founder, who built the chipmaker into one of the most valuable businesses on the planet, is forced out. Shares of Nvidia sank more than 4% on Monday, even as the broader market rallied sharply, after Huang acknowledged the affair in a message to staff on Sunday, and said that the board was launching an investigation into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence agency. The board said it has "confidence in Jensen," and that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." The New York Times first reported that the Chinese businesswoman was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence circulated in a memo among the Trump administration in the spring. China has called the allegation a smear. While Nvidia says Huang will continue to lead the company during the probe, pressure is rapidly mounting on the chipmaker, whose technology has powered the first four years of the generative artificial intelligence boom. Leaders from both parties are calling for briefings, and Democrats poised to take control of both houses of Congress are calling for investigations and new legislation "to stop advanced AI chips from fueling China's military," Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts wrote in a post on X on Monday. Huang has outsized influence over Nvidia, and is the sole face of the company with no clear second-in-command. He's also among the loudest champions of AI in the country, is critical to the financing of the broader infrastructure buildout and has a close relationship with President Donald Trump , giving Nvidia a front-row seat when it comes to discussions on AI policy, safety and regulation. "The issue at Nvidia is that there is no clear successor to Jensen, and we had expected him to stay in this role for at least 10 more years," analysts at Melius Research said in a Monday research note. Stacy Rasgon, an analyst at Bernstein, told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Monday that, "Jensen is Nvidia. Nvidia is Jensen." He added that Huang "runs the thing pretty much top down," and "sort of pulls all the strings." Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Nvidia has long maintained a flat, non-hierarchical organizational structure. Huang has deep involvement in the company's day-to-day operations and frequently serves as its spokesperson in front of world leaders and at industry conferences. In addition to being co-founder and CEO, Huang is also Nvidia's president. In September of 2025, Huang told CNBC's Becky Quick that he had as many as 60 direct reports. Internal records reviewed by CNBC reveal that, as of this week, he had 33 direct reports, including CFO Colette Kress, influential Chief Scientist Bill Dally, senior vice president of software engineering Dwight Diercks, and Ian Buck, best known as the inventor of Nvidia's CUDA software. However, relative to some of his founder peers in tech like Meta's Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk at SpaceX , Huang has minimal actual control. He owns just over 3% of the outstanding shares and is one of 11 members on a board that has no official chair. And in the risk factors of Nvidia's financial filings , Huang isn't specifically identified as a key person. Rather, the company says, "we are highly dependent on the services of our longstanding executive team." "Failure to ensure effective succession planning, transfer of knowledge, and smooth transitions involving executives and key employees could hinder our strategic planning, execution, and long-term success," Nvidia says. Still, Huang's influence is undeniable, so much so that the question of succession is one that's hardly broached among analysts and investors. Timm Schulze-Melander, an analyst at Rothschild & Co. Redburn, wrote in a Monday note that Huang could be forced to step back from the CEO role if the board's investigation reveals "something materially more serious" than an undisclosed relationship. But Schulze-Melander said Huang's potential resignation isn't a foregone conclusion of the investigation, pointing to the importance of his leadership at the company. Nvidia's board "needs to demonstrate independence and protect shareholders without destabilizing a company whose success is unusually dependent on its founder," Schulze-Melander wrote. "Its initial statement suggests it is attempting to achieve both." Several analysts said the investigation could lead to governance changes at Nvidia, including putting a transition contingency plan in place. The Melius analysts wrote that Nvidia has a "strong bench" of executive talent across its networking, hyperscale and high-performance computing businesses, along with "technical expertise" stemming from Chief Technology Officer Michael Kagan as well as Dally, the chief scientist. "While these folks can keep the engine running, Jensen is one of a kind, and his energy will be needed to maintain confidence in the AI trade," the analysts wrote. — CNBC's Kif Leswing, Kristina Partsinevelos and Michael Bloom contributed to this report. According to a complaint filed in federal court in San Jose, ​California, the Nvidia and Huang misled shareholders in connection with the executive’s alleged ​affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based ⁠Megaspeed who is not related to him. Nvidia did not immediately respond to ​a request for comment to Reuters. sources.text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has never been quiet about his belief that the U.S. should continue selling AI chips to China, rather than shutting the country off from the technology. The revelation that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy threatens to complicate that argument. The Financial Times reported Friday on Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized in a memo to the company on Sunday. U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the CEO and influence the company’s efforts to loosen chip export restrictions. Nvidia’s independent directors, working with outside legal counsel, are investigating the matter, and Congress is already demanding answers . The controversy comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia. Historically, China has been a big market for the company. It has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives. In the three months ended July 26, Nvidia recorded $7.9 billion in revenue from customers headquartered in China, roughly 8% of total revenue. Huang has repeatedly lobbied the U.S. government to expand access to China , and some of his persuasion tactics have been successful. Huang met repeatedly with President Donald Trump and administration officials last year; afterward, the government reversed restrictions on Nvidia’s H20 chips and allowed exports of its more powerful H200 processors. On numerous occasions, Huang has publicly lamented export controls, calling them a “ failure ” at a conference last year and saying in May that it was “ not wise ” for the U.S. and China to create two distinct AI ecosystems. He has also warned that shutting Nvidia out of China’s compute market would enable the country to develop its own AI chips to challenge Nvidia internationally. China is already moving in that direction. Reuters reported last week that about 600,000 H200 chips are being held in Hong Kong, awaiting shipment to mainland China. Beijing is pushing AI companies to prioritize buying chips from Chinese companies instead. The idea that Huang needed any encouragement in the form of an attractive woman to push for greater access to China seems like a stretch, particularly because his lobbying efforts predate their reported meeting at an Nvidia event in early 2024. At the end of the day, Huang is a salesman trying to dominate one of the world’s biggest AI markets. Still, the allegations involving Alice Huang open new scrutiny of the company’s business relationships and could taint any assurances Nvidia offers that it can prevent sensitive technology from reaching unauthorized customers. Once made, rumors of questionable allegiances can be hard to shake. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly warned officials close to Trump earlier this year about Huang’s relationship with an alleged spy. Even if Nvidia’s investigation finds that Huang didn’t share secrets with his paramour, the question is whether he’ll be able to convince Washington that Nvidia can still responsibly do business with China. sources.title: Trump stands by Nvidia boss Jensen Huang despite spy scandal, but FBI is investigating
sources.text: The revelations this weekend that Nvidia Corp. boss Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman who has been accused of working for Chinese intelligence have now ensnared U.S. President Donald Trump, raising further questions about national security. At the same time, the Federal Bureau of Investigation said it’s looking into the affair, meaning it’s likely to get continuing attention in coming weeks or longer. Nvidia said it has launched an investigation into Chief Executive Huang’s actions after he admitted to cheating on his wife with a woman known as Alice Huang (no relation), who serves as the CEO of a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed . U.S. intelligence officials suspect Alice Huang has been feeding information about Huang and the chipmaker’s plans to the Chinese government. And though Trump was informed of the possible infiltration, he has continued working with Nvidia and Huang on domestic policy issues related to technology and artificial intelligence, which have become of vital importance to the U.S. economy. Huang has spent the last two years cultivating a close relationship with Trump, gaining extraordinary access to America’s top decision-maker and influence over the country’s AI strategy. He has gone from being virtually unknown to the president to being a key member of a cadre of technology industry executives accompanying him on trips aboard Air Force One, including a visit to China in May. He has come to be seen as a major ally of Trump, attending numerous White House events while repeatedly praising his policies. Notably, his company made a $25 million donation to the president’s gaudy ballroom project, becoming its top corporate contributor alongside Apple Inc. Those efforts seem to have gone a long way toward getting Huang into the president’s good graces, and it seems to have paid off for the company. Last year, after months of lobbying from Huang and Nvidia, the Trump administration agreed that it could sell more advanced chips to China that were previously banned from being exported to the country. Though that decision was widely known, it seems that the Trump administration has intervened in other ways to protect Nvidia’s interests. Earlier today, the New York Times reported that a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed, which was suspected of smuggling banned chips into China, was abruptly canceled after receiving an email from Nvidia’s general counsel. Commerce official Jeff Kessler, who was nominated for the role by Trump, reportedly gave Nvidia permission to contact the investigation team and mention his name, which goes against standard protocol. Investigators had grown suspicious that Megaspeed was essentially just a front for smuggling embargoed Nvidia chips into China, but the correspondence from Nvidia’s general counsel Tim Teter kicked off a kerfuffle that ultimately led to the investigation being transferred to the Department of Justice. But Trump defended Huang late on Sunday, stating that the Nvidia boss is an “honorable guy” who has not committed any wrongdoing. The president had been briefed about the suspected Chinese intelligence operation as far back as October 2025, but decided not to do anything , according to the Times. “I haven’t heard that he’s done anything wrong,” Trump said. “He dealt with somebody, but, you know, so does everybody else.” Trump continued to defend Huang on Monday when quizzed about the situation again, before revealing that the Federal Bureau of Investigation is also looking into his relationship with the suspected spy. “I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he’ll be in good shape,” he said at a White House briefing. Despite the apparent protection afforded by Trump, Huang appears to be taking no chances. A report in Wired said today that the Nvidia boss has hired the services of a public relations firm called Heller that specializes in handling public scandals. Rise Heller, the firm’s founder, has developed a reputation for helping powerful men sidestep allegations of sexual misconduct and other personal controversies. She previously represented clients including the former Congressman Anthony Weiner, the writer Jeffrey Toobin and the chef Mario Batali, Wired reported. Tech industry personalities have also leapt to Huang’s defense. Shaun Maguire, a partner at the venture capital firm Sequoia Capital said in a post on X that Huang is “one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation,” and stressed that although he did something “incredibly dumb,” he believes there was “no bad intention.” Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk later shared Maguire’s post, saying he agrees with all of it. However, no intervention has managed to protect Nvidia’s stock, which slid more than 4% on Monday , wiping around $190 billion off of the company’s valuation. Nvidia is scheduled to hold its next financial earnings call on Nov. 17, in which Huang is likely to face some very difficult questions — if he is on the call as has been customary. In this post, we cover what’s new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with the model on Amazon Bedrock. Fable 5.2 raises the bar on the hardest problems in coding, math, and science. It takes on ambiguous, multi-step work, verifies its own output, and can run unattended for hours to days. It interprets prompts, iterates, catches its own errors, and optimizes as it goes. In Anthropic’s alignment testing, Mythos 5.2 hallucinates less, completes tasks more reliably, surfaces important information more consistently, and self-reports issues more honestly than Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1. Anthropic expects Fable 5.2 to behave similarly. If a cyber security query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 4.8, and if a biology query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 5. On Amazon Bedrock, the retry is your code’s job, not an automatic switch. If the declined request hit the prompt cache, the refusal also includes a fallback credit token. Send that token with the retry and it’s billed as cache reads, so you don’t pay to write the same cache twice. Check the documentation for more information on fallback credit. For authorized work in cyber security and life sciences, Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs . Mythos 5.2 covers two high-risk domains, available only through the verification programs noted earlier: Anthropic designates Claude Fable 5.2 as a Covered Model . By default, its use requires retention for up to 30 days and human safety review. On Amazon Bedrock, Amazon personnel perform the review within the AWS boundary. Set the aws_review data retention mode on your account or project before you invoke the model. See Amazon Bedrock data retention for more details. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), built in collaboration with AWS, combines the privacy of zero data retention (ZDR) with state-of-the-art safeguards for detecting misuse. EFS works by storing data in cloud infrastructure controlled by the customer. Until EFS is available, eligible customers can use Fable 5.2 with zero data retention. This is available for internal use through at least June 30, 2027. To try Fable 5.2, open the Amazon Bedrock console , choose Test , Playground , and select Fable 5.2 as the model. From there, you can run a prompt directly against it. Programmatically, you can call the model with the Anthropic Messages API against bedrock-runtime (through the Anthropic SDK). You can also stay on the Invoke and Converse APIs on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK . To follow along with the code examples in this post, you need the following: Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3): You can explore the Getting Started notebook for more examples. For teams already running Claude models on Amazon Bedrock, the claude-api skill in Claude Code helps you upgrade to Fable 5.2. The claude-api skill is an open-source skill built into Claude Code that captures the details that make Claude API code work well. It covers which agent patterns fit a given job, what parameters change between model generations, and when to apply prompt caching. It stays current as Anthropic’s SDKs evolve: when a new model is released or the API gains a feature, the skill already knows. When you ask Claude Code to upgrade your codebase to Fable 5.2, the skill reviews your code and walks you through: The skill also detects your deployment platform including Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, and other environments and adjusts model ID formats and feature configurations accordingly. For example, it uses the Amazon Bedrock structured model ID format ( global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-2 ). In Claude Code, run the migration directly: This scans your working directory (or a subdirectory or specific file list you confirm) and applies the migration changes in a single guided pass. You can also invoke it conversationally by telling Claude Code: The claude-api skill is available in Claude Code and is also bundled into CodeRabbit, JetBrains IDEs (including Junie), Resolve AI, and Warp. It is open source at anthropics/skills on GitHub, so any coding agent can integrate it. sources.text: Anthropic debuted Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on Monday, the company’s answer to OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, which came out in early September. The new models, which could be Anthropic’s last big releases before its IPO, claim to offer higher performance than Astra at a lower price point—a key factor for earning and retaining customers in a world where professionals seem quick to switch to models based on cost, as long as the performance holds up. The launch is critical for Anthropic as it seeks to re-accelerate revenue growth, following a third quarter slowdown revealed in latest S-1 filing with the SEC. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are 20% cheaper than Astra for ordinary input and output tasks, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, compared to $10 and $50, respectively, for GPT-6 Astra. Tokens are the unit of information AI model process. One token of English language text is equivalent to about a word-and-a-half. For prompts with large amounts of information, such as documents, the cost advantage is more pronounced. Anthropic’s new models are 80% cheaper, at 20 cents per million cached tokens compared to one dollar per million cached tokens for GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic reports impressive results from its pre-release testing. The new models “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications,” the company said. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 perform better than its competitors on coding evaluation benchmarks, Anthropic said, noting that over 90% of the company’s own code is written by AI. While Anthropic’s Claude Code product gained an early lead among programmers, OpenAI’s Codex has gained ground in recent months due to its lower pricing, The Information reported in late October. The combination of lower pricing plus superior performance, if the company’s claims hold up in real-world testing, could help win them back. The new models are best when used for the “most ambitious, open-ended technical work,” Anthropic said. In other words, they’re competing with Astra at the frontier. However, for daily tasks, Anthropic recommends its customers use its more cost-effective model, Opus 5.5. That model is more expensive than its direct competitor from OpenAI, GPT-6.1 Sol, although it still could end up being a better deal if it yields a high quality result more often. That’s for users to decide as they inevitably begin to try Anthropic’s latest releases and weigh options on a daily basis. Anthropic is also trying to compete with OpenAI on cybersecurity tasks, such as finding and fixing vulnerabilities in code. The company claims an unnamed security company “found that one in six confirmed bugs found by Claude Mythos 5.2 were missed by all of the other frontier models they tested.” Late last week, OpenAI debuted a cybersecurity-focused model, GPT-6 Cyber . The new Anthropic models also reportedly solved two theoretical physics problems related to black holes, and identified a way to speed up research into gene therapies. In light of OpenAI making headlines for solving mathematics proofs that have eluded academics for decades—most notably the 90-year-old Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem—Anthropic is highlighting its new models’ mathematics chops as well. A team of 1,000 agents powerd by Fable 5.2 produced a formalization, or translation of a mathematical proof into a format a computer can check step by step, in 30 hours, compared with 11 days for a previous, unreleased research version of Claude. In a subtle jab at the mathematics community’s backlash to OpenAI pouring millions of dollars into solving proofs and upending the field, Anthropic notes that its quick formalizations can help human mathematicians check their proofs faster so they can “spend more time exploring novel ideas.” One unique area Anthropic seems to be leaning into more than OpenAI is hardware and robotics. The new models were allegedly able to design and produce three working electronic devices, complete with circuit boards, 3D-printed enclosures, and software, based on a one-paragraph prompt. Finally, Anthropic highlighted the models’ safety features, including safeguards that block “high-risk cyber activities including penetration testing, exploit generation, and binary-based vulnerability, as well as most tasks in research biology.” Claude Fable 5.2 is available today on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. Mythos 5.2 access is application-only for cybersecurity professionals and life sciences researchers . Claude Enterprise customers can also access Mythos 5.2 through Anthropic’s Claude Security product.

sources.text: Anthropic released new versions of its most advanced models on Monday, with the launch of Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2. sources.text: Anthropic PBC today pulled back the curtains on Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, its two most capable large language models to date. The LLMs are identical as far as their core capabilities are concerned. The difference is that Fable 5.2 blocks certain biology and cybersecurity use cases, while Mythos 5.2 includes more relaxed guardrails. The latter model is only available to trusted researchers through a pair of limited-access programs. Anthropic tested Fable 5.2 against its predecessor across 14 artificial intelligence benchmarks. The model beat Fable 5.1’s score by more than 10% across most of the tests. It’s particularly adept at scientific research: Fable 5.2 scored 74.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, a 22% improvement over Fable 5.1. Earlier this year, Anthropic used an unreleased LLM to generate a computer-verifiable version of a famous mathematical proof. The project took 11 days. According to Anthropic, Fable 5.2 reduced the workflow to 30 hours by spinning up 1,000 agents to parallelize calculations. In a separate project, it answered two open questions about a theoretical physics concept related to black holes. The company also tested Mythos 5.2, the invite-only version of Fable 5.2. It asked the model to study the protective shells of harmless viruses called AAVs. AAV shells, or capsids as they’re known in scientific parlance, are used by some therapies to deliver drugs. Mythos 5.2 accurately modeled the structure of 28 out of the 34 AAV capsids it studied. The result is notable because capsids comprise dozens of different proteins. Other cutting-edge models that are optimized for biology research, notably Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold2, can only model the structure of individual proteins. The creators of the latter model won one half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry. Fable 5.2 includes guardrails that block most research biology questions and many cybersecurity-related prompts. If users enter a request that falls into either of those categories, the model sends it to Opus 4.8 or Opus 5. Anthropic says Fable 5.2 is 55% less likely to erroneously block safe prompts than Fable 5.1. The model outperforms its predecessor by more than 13% across two coding benchmarks called FrontierCode 2.0 FrontierSWE 2.0. According to Anthropic, one of its engineers put the model’s programming capabilities to the test by asking it to build an operating system. Fable 5.2 spun up up 1,000 agents that completed the task in about eight days. The operating system they created can run on a laptop, offers network access and features a Claude sidebar. Anthropic sees customers using Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 to speed up highly complicated, open-ended technical tasks. The company says more day-to-day workflows can be automated more efficiently using Opus 5.5, an LLM it introduced in July. Users can also combine the models by having Opus 5.5 ask Fable 5.2 or Mythos 5.2 for advise when it encounters a bottleneck. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. That makes them 20% more affordable than Anthropic’s previous-generation models. Both LLMs offer a high-performance mode that generates prompt responses 2.5 times faster than the standard tier for double the price. sources.text: Huang built Nvidia as a family business but after the co-founder had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, its board faces a difficult decision For more than 30 years, Jensen Huang has been the seemingly unshakable public face of Nvidia. He co-founded the company as a young engineer in 1993 and oversaw its growth into a multitrillion dollar chipmaker and bellwether of the AI industry at large. He’s also made it a family business. His children, Madison and Spencer, have taken leadership roles at the firm. While not a company executive, his wife, Lori Mills Huang, leads the family foundation which, as of 2024, controls over 60m Nvidia shares. But Huang’s image as a family man has been shattered as of Sunday. After the New York Times revealed at the end of October that Huang may have been targeted by a Chinese intelligence asset who he had developed a close relationship with, he admitted in a letter to employees on Sunday that he had been having an affair. Initially , Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said there was nothing out of the ordinary about Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang , an executive at a Singaporean datacenter firm, Megaspeed. US government officials had suspected Huang of smuggling American chips into China, prompting those officials to surveil and monitor her, the Times first reported. In the course of that surveillance, officials allegedly determined that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy and had gotten close with the Nvidia leader. Nvidia’s board of directors have now launched an independent investigation about the national security concerns surrounding Huang’s relationship. “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully,” Huang wrote in his letter. “I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” Megaspeed did not respond to a Guardian request for comment before publication. In his letter, Huang apologized to his family, acknowledging how much they’ve supported him. His wife, Mills, kept a relatively low profile and didn’t play a formal role at Nvidia. However, in a 2023 interview with the New Yorker, Huang shared that Mills had also worked in Silicon Valley as a microchips engineer before stepping away to raise their children. “Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support,” Huang wrote in his letter to employees. “They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.” Both his children now hold high ranking roles at the company, despite not initially pursuing careers in tech. His daughter, Madison, serves as the senior director of product and technical marketing for physical AI platforms, but got her start as a chef. She attended the Culinary Institute of America and Le Cordon Bleu before going to business school and transitioning to luxury marketing. She previously worked at LVMH – the parent company of Lous Vuitton. Spencer , for his part, now serves as the director of product for Robotics at Nvidia but spent much of his career as a consultant before joining his father’s company as a product manager. Before consulting, he owned and co-founded a craft cocktail bar in Taiwan. In his letter, Huang reiterated his commitment to Nvidia, saying he hoped to earn back his colleagues’ and employees’ trust. However, analysts and investors say there’s a chance he may be removed as CEO after the board’s investigation. “This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons,” said Dan Ives, a partner and analyst at investment bank Yorkville Ives. “There is clearly risk as discussed that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally.” Ives said the family’s role at Nvidia adds some complexities for the board. “The board has to make its decision independent of the family spider web of Jensen and his family at Nvidia,” Ives told the Guardian. “It makes this a very complex situation for the board to navigate with the world watching.” Huang is to Nvidia what Steve Jobs was to Apple, said Ken Mahoney, the CEO and president of Mahoney Asset Management. “If you asked any Nvidia investor or anyone involved in tech and markets, would they like to see Jensen gone? Definitely not, but [Nvidia] would survive,” Mahoney said. “Losing Huang would introduce a lot of uncertainty, particularly given his influence over Nvidia’s strategy, culture, and relationships with major technology companies,” he continued. “The bigger question is whether a successor could maintain Huang’s strategic vision and ability to anticipate where the industry is heading, and how that new leader could be tested along the way if things become difficult.” Executive affairs or inappropriate relationships have recently unseated CEOs, according to executive recruiting and coaching firm Challenger Gray and Christmas. In 2024, the CEO of Astronomer was caught on a kiss cam with the company’s chief people officer, leading him to resign shortly after. Nestlé fired CEO Laurent Freixe for a relationship with a subordinate. Nvidia offers a more complex picture. sources.title: Google lança novos chips de IA para aumentar segurança e poder computacional
sources.text: Por André Lourenti Magalhães • Editado por Jones Oliveira | 09/11/2026 às 10:00 O Google Cloud anunciou dois novos TPUs para a infraestrutura de IA nesta segunda-feira (09). De olho nos impactos dos agentes de IA no uso computacional, a empresa traz soluções para aumentar a segurança de dados e permitir janelas de contexto massivas. O TPU 8tx tem o objetivo de trazer inferências mais seguras e segurança computacional a nível de hardware. O chip é ideal para empresas que precisam tratar e treinar dados confidenciais e conta com hosts CPU personalizados da AMD para garantir que as informações sejam armazenadas com segurança. Já o TPU 8i Max foi criado para acabar com possíveis gargalos de memória no processamento de IA e permitir trabalhos em larga escala . O chip tem suporte a janelas de contexto massivas, aumenta a largura de banda da memória para transmissão de dados e permite maior densidade computacional (maior poder de computação por metro quadrado e por watt). Os novos componentes ampliam a linha de TPUs do Google: a linha de 8ª geração foi anunciada em abril deste ano com os modelos TPU 8i e TPU 8t . O Google informa que o aumento do uso de agentes de IA foi um dos fatores para a criação de novos chips. O salto da escala humana para a escala agêntica exige maior poder computacional, especialmente pelo fato de que um bot pode criar fluxos de trabalho complexos e contínuos. “Com a computação migrando da escala humana para a escala de agentes, as empresas estão pedindo aceleradores que possam raciocinar sobre as massivas janelas de contexto dos modelos de IA. Além disso, alguns clientes, altamente regulamentados, estão pedindo recursos de criptografia especializados para cargas de trabalho únicas”, explica o Diretor de Tecnologia e Vice-Presidente Sênior de IA e Infraestrutura do Google, Amin Vahdat. Sigla para Tensor Processing Unit (“Unidade de processamento de tensor”, em tradução livre), TPU é um chip desenvolvido pelo Google para uso em aprendizado de máquina e infraestrutura de IA . O componente é usado em data centers e permite maior poder de computação para inferência no treinamento de modelos .

sources.text: O Google anunciou nesta segunda-feira (9) o TPU 8i Max e o TPU 8tx , dois novos chips de inteligência artificial (IA) destinados ao aprimoramento de tarefas realizadas por agentes autônomos em meio à ampla implementação desses sistemas no setor produtivo. As novidades se juntam às outras duas configurações de 8ª geração lançadas este ano . “Com a computação migrando da escala humana para a escala de agentes, as empresas estão pedindo aceleradores que possam raciocinar sobre as massivas janelas de contexto dos modelos de IA. Além disso, alguns clientes, altamente regulamentados, estão pedindo recursos de criptografia especializados para cargas de trabalho únicas”, afirmou Amin Vahdat, Diretor de Tecnologia e Vice-Presidente Sênior de IA e Infraestrutura do Google, em comunicado. Integrando a segurança diretamente na camada de hardware, o TPU 8tx mantém dados sensíveis e pesos de modelos protegidos e isolados mesmo durante o uso ativo , de acordo com a companhia. Além disso, apresenta latência duas vezes menor na comparação com a versão 8t anunciada em abril. Já o TPU 8i Max foi projetado para lidar com eventuais gargalos de memória que podem surgir ao executar dezenas de agentes de uma só vez. Ele disponibiliza o dobro de poder computacional, de SRAM e da largura de banda de HBM do TPU 8i, trazendo fluidez para grandes cargas de trabalho. A novidade também acomoda o dobro de silício dentro da mesma estrutura, permitindo que data centers implantem significativamente mais poder de computação por metro quadrado e por watt, como explicou a big tech. A Unidade de Processamento Tensorial (TPU) é utilizada de diferentes maneiras pela gigante das buscas. A tecnologia aprimora o treinamento de modelos próprios da companhia para cargas de trabalho de agentes , por exemplo, disponibilizando-os para clientes do Google Cloud . Usuários da infraestrutura em nuvem também podem implantar os TPUs em seus data centers, diante do aumento da demanda. sources.title: CEO da Nvidia admite traição em meio a escândalo de espionagem chinesa
sources.text: Por Raphael Giannotti | 09/11/2026 às 14:08 A NVIDIA atravessa agora seu pior momento envolvendo a vida pessoal do CEO, Jensen Huang, e possível espionagem por brecha aberta por ele mesmo. Em nota pública, o executivo admitiu uma traição e pediu desculpas por isso à sua família. Ao mesmo tempo, o conselho administrativo da gigante americana abriu uma investigação independente para saber se o caso extraconjugal resultou em espionagem por parte da China . A crise ganhou contornos dramáticos após reportagens do The New York Times e do Financial Times apontarem que o r elacionamento extraconjugal de Huang envolveu Alice Huang (que não é parente), executiva da empresa Megaspeed, cliente sediada em Singapura que adquiriu mais de US$ 4,8 bilhões em chips da NVIDIA nos últimos dois anos e que estaria sob suspeita de repassar informações estratégicas à inteligência de Pequim . Em uma mensagem enviada aos funcionários da companhia, Jensen Huang assumiu total responsabilidade pelo escândalo pessoal. "Fui infiel à minha esposa. Minhas ações machucaram ela e nossos filhos. Não há desculpa para o que fiz. Sinto muito", escreveu o CEO, pedindo privacidade para sua família e reafirmando seu compromisso de continuar à frente da fabricante e cooperar integralmente com as apurações . Apesar da postura do executivo, o conselho de administração agiu rápido ao emitir uma nota oficial confirmando o início de uma auditoria independente sobre o caso . A mesa diretora enfatizou que, no momento, "não há razões para acreditar que a segurança nacional dos EUA ou os segredos industriais da NVIDIA foram comprometidos" , mas destacou que os interesses de segurança geopolítica estão acima de quaisquer objetivos corporativos. A investigação conduzida pelo conselho examina minuciosamente o contexto e o timing por trás das revelações para determinar se a vulnerabilidade pessoal do CEO foi intencionalmente explorada por agentes de inteligência chineses em um esquema de "armadilha amorosa". A situação é extremamente delicada por acontecer no auge da disputa entre Washington e Pequim pela hegemonia da inteligência artificial. Sendo a NVIDIA o motor principal dos aceleradores mais avançados e valiosos do planeta, o conselho da empresa busca garantir que a propriedade intelectual e os chips de altíssimo desempenho da marca continuem blindados contra vazamentos ou interferências governamentais externas.

sources.title: DeepSeek Harness cresce 545% e alcança 1,54 milhão de usuários
sources.text: A plataforma DeepSeek Harness, voltada à criação e operação de agentes de inteligência artificial , alcançou 1,54 milhão de usuários diários e processa 92,1 trilhões de tokens a cada 24 horas, segundo dados oficiais divulgados pela startup chinesa no X. O crescimento foi impulsionado pelo lançamento da versão para computadores. A plataforma também soma 5,48 milhões de usuários ativos mensais e registra uma média de 261 requisições diárias por pessoa. Em poucas semanas, a quantidade de usuários ativos por dia aumentou 545%. No mesmo período, o consumo de tokens chegou a 92,1 trilhões por dia, alta de 306%. Tokens são unidades básicas utilizadas pelos modelos de inteligência artificial para processar e gerar informações. Entre os modelos associados à expansão está o V4.5-Flash. A comunidade de desenvolvedores também participa da expansão do ambiente. O Harness já reúne quase 35 mil plugins de terceiros, dos quais aproximadamente 30 mil estão hospedados no GitHub . Cerca de 59% dos usuários ativos constroem ou utilizam pelo menos uma extensão para automatizar atividades de trabalho. Conhecido pela sigla DSH, o DeepSeek Harness é uma estrutura de código aberto voltada à operação de agentes autônomos. Esses sistemas conseguem executar tarefas no computador sem depender de comandos humanos a cada etapa. Sob o lema “tudo é um plugin”, a plataforma permite que desenvolvedores externos adicionem ferramentas e recursos ao ambiente. A proposta é transformá-la em uma espécie de sistema operacional para agentes de inteligência artificial, no qual diferentes extensões ampliam as capacidades do assistente. Os números divulgados, porém, representam apenas o ecossistema do Harness, sem incluir os usuários do chat convencional da DeepSeek. Também não devem ser comparados diretamente aos indicadores de outros assistentes, que utilizam períodos diferentes de medição. O ChatGPT, por exemplo, registra mais de 1,2 bilhão de usuários semanais, enquanto o Claude também mantém presença entre os principais serviços do setor. Entre os recursos que podem ser incorporados à plataforma estão: Para ampliar o ecossistema, a startup anunciou a criação de um marketplace próprio, dedicado à descoberta e instalação de plugins. A iniciativa também prevê incentivos para desenvolvedores independentes e empresas interessadas em criar ferramentas para a plataforma. O programa deverá oferecer créditos gratuitos de computação, chamados de token grants, além de suporte técnico. Com essas medidas, a DeepSeek pretende estimular a criação de novas extensões e ampliar a participação de terceiros no desenvolvimento do Harness. Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.
